::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [late June or early July] 1884.  
**From:** Otterbourne,  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  This fragment printed in [<i>Dulce Domum</i>](other_books/otherbook_122.qmd), 279.
:::

[To [Mary Ann Moberly](people/person_1019.qmd)]

How little I thought when I met dear [Joanna Patteson](people/person_1154.qmd) in your drawing-room that it was the last time I should see her!  [Fanny Patteson](people/person_1151.qmd) had come back, and is sure Joan knew and was thinking for others to the last. . . .   I hope you are profiting by the splendid summer weather.  I never knew a year of sweeter smells:  the sheets of wild honeysuckle are quite amazing . . .

---

**Note:** Joanna Elizabeth Patteson (1818/9-23 June 1884) was the elder half-sister of Fanny Patteson and of [Bishop Patteson](people/person_1155.qmd).
